title: Sanitizing delivery notes, search terms and menu uploads
name: Delivery input handling

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code sanitizes and handles user-supplied input? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Searching for restaurants with q="100%" is bound as a query parameter. Why does like_contains also escape the term and why does the SQL add ESCAPE?
choices: Binding already stops injection, and without escaping the percent sign would additionally act as a wildcard, so the escaping makes the term match literally
The escaping prevents SQL injection, because bound parameters are only quoted, not validated
ESCAPE makes SQLite compare case-insensitively for non-ASCII text
The backslashes are required so that sqlite3 can convert the Python str into bytes

questions.prompt: search_restaurants builds the ORDER BY clause with an f-string. Why is that acceptable here?
choices: SQLite ignores quotes and semicolons inside an ORDER BY clause
The sort value is truncated to 20 characters by clean_text before use
The string is placed after the LIMIT placeholder, so it cannot change the query
Only strings from the ORDER_BY dict can be interpolated, and the dict key is restricted to three literal values by the model, so user text never reaches the SQL

questions.prompt: Delivery notes are stored after clean_text but are HTML-escaped only when the slip is rendered, and are prefixed only when exported to CSV. What is the reasoning?
choices: Escaping on write would be safer, and the render-time escaping is redundant
Stored text keeps its meaning, and each output sink applies the encoding that fits its own context (HTML or spreadsheet formulas)
clean_text already removes angle brackets, so html.escape only matters for ampersands
The slip endpoint is authenticated, so it can trust stored text
